newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close much stronger, outperform U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close much stronger, outperform U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Thursday, with spreads to U.S. Treasuries narrowing, as weak U.S. data and optimism about the upcoming federal budget drove prices higher, analysts said.

"It's a good day to be a bull. The big factor on the day was the U.S. data," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with I.D.E.A. "Canada continued to outperform again. That's mainly due to the fact that the U.S. had a lot of supply this week and there's increased optimism going into the budget.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$1.70 to C$113.60 to yield 6.873 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 31/32 to yield 6.63 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds shrank to 24 basis points from 29 basis points at Wednesday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened this morning after a report that U.S. retail sales rose 0.6 percent in January and 0.4 percent excluding autos. Retail sales had been expected to rise by 0.7 percent overall and by 0.6 percent including autos.
Analysts said Canadian bonds are also benefitting from optimism surrounding the upcoming federal budget, which will be released on Tuesday.
"The government is probably going to keep on track, on the straight and narrow," said Kalirai.

Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Thursday predicted Canada would probably do better than its budget deficit targets for the current fiscal year and next fiscal year, but pledged that his government will not relax its fiscal discipline.

Canadian bonds also saw narrowing spreads to U.S. issues as the U.S. market this afternoon faced the final leg of its quarterly refunding, the auction of US$10 billion in 30-year notes. The results of the auction were described by analysts as unexceptional.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$1.08 to C$105.95 to yield 6.179 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 16/32 to yield 6.31 percent. The spread between the bonds was 13 basis points.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.83 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.12 percent.
